items.title: The first backward return of a centre to a symmetric subinterval lands on a centre or on an endpoint
items.author: Przemyslaw Berk; Frank Trujillo
items.work: Ergodic properties of infinite extension of symmetric interval exchange transformations
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled claim at source lines 761-775: for a centre other than the distinguished one, with first backward return time to the symmetric subinterval equal to l, either the orbit fragment up to the shifted exponent avoids the discontinuities and the projected point is a centre of the induced transformation satisfying an explicit identity, or that fragment meets the discontinuities and the projected point is an endpoint of the induced transformation while the centre lies in a non-trivial connection. The proof (source lines 777-800) runs the two alternatives with genuinely different arguments: in the first, the shift by the indicator has to be carried through the backward-iterate formula and the local reflection lemma before the projected point can be recognised as a fixed point of the conjugate of the induced transformation; in the second, the first meeting with the discontinuities has to be located before the connection criterion applies. The statement records the two alternatives and neither mechanism.
